title: Best Cat Carriers UK
short: Cat carriers compared by comfort, ventilation and ease of getting your cat in and out, from budget soft carriers to crash-tested car seats.
intro: A good cat carrier makes vet trips and travel dramatically less stressful for both of you, and the number and position of doors matters as much as size. This guide compares carriers tested hands-on by PetsRadar's team on their own cats, with veterinary input from Dr Hannah Godfrey.

products.name: Expandable Pet Carrier
products.best_for: Longer journeys where your cat needs room to stretch out
products.key_spec: Expandable sides add 10in on each end, 5 doors, removable base
products.summary: Gives cats plenty of room to move once unzipped, with an extra 10 inches on both ends for stretching out on longer journeys, and folds away to save space when not in use. PetsRadar's tester found it lightweight to carry yet comfortable for her cat, with five doors making vet examinations easier without a full removal.
pros: Expandable for extra space on longer trips
Easy to fold away and store

products.name: Maeve
products.best_for: Buyers who want a crash-tested, multi-use carrier
products.key_spec: 3-in-1 stroller/car seat/bed, UN ECE crash-test certified, UPF 50+ canopy
products.summary: Converts between a stroller, car seat and cosy bed, secured in the car with its own base and stability leg. PetsRadar's tester said her cat barely gets out of it since it arrived, praising the easy-to-clean materials and swappable interior, though the instructions are tricky to follow and it's the priciest option.

specs.Safety: UN ECE Child Restraint Standard crash-tested

products.name: Two Door Top Load Plastic Dog & Cat Kennel
products.best_for: Shy cats who want privacy, or multi-cat households
products.key_spec: 95% recycled plastic, top-load door, airline approved
products.summary: Made from durable recycled plastic that's quick to wipe clean and suits cats who chew or scratch, with enough coverage to give shy cats privacy. PetsRadar's tester loved the top-loading door for placing resistant cats inside, and found it big enough for two cats at once despite being surprisingly light.
cons: Harder to store than a soft carrier
Might be too big for smaller cats

products.name: Cat Carrier with Wheels
products.best_for: Air travel or long walks through busy airports
products.key_spec: Detachable trolley, 360° spinning wheels, airline approved
products.summary: A detachable trolley with a retractable handle and 360°-spinning wheels makes moving through an airport far easier than carrying by strap. PetsRadar found it airline-approved with breathable mesh ventilation, foldable for storage, though it costs more than other soft carriers in the guide.
cons: More expensive than other soft carriers

products.name: Signature Dog & Cat Car Seat & Carrier Bag
products.best_for: Cats who like to see out during car journeys
products.key_spec: Mesh windows on sides, top and front, seatbelt attachment, interior tether
products.summary: A soft-fabric carrier with mesh windows on three sides for cats who like to look around, plus a fleecy base pad. PetsRadar found it works well for car journeys thanks to seatbelt attachment and an interior tether, with a rear storage pouch for treats or vet paperwork, though it isn't foldable or crash-tested.
pros: Mesh windows for ventilation and visibility

products.name: Portable Pet Travel Carrier
products.best_for: Budget-conscious owners who still want the essential features
products.key_spec: Under £30, removable base, long strap, name card for vet details
products.summary: Covers all the basic features needed at a low price, with a long strap alternative to the short handles and a name card for filling in vet details. PetsRadar's tester liked the two doors for curious cats and the foldable design for easy storage, noting only that the base pad is a little hard without an added blanket.
cons: Base pad is a little hard without extra padding

guide.a: Soft carriers, like the Pet Gear or Bella & Pal here, are lighter, foldable and often more comfortable for nervous cats, while hard carriers, like the Frisco, give more structural protection and are easier to wipe clean, which particularly suits cats who chew or scratch at fabric.

guide.q: How many doors do I actually need?
guide.a: A single-door carrier is fine for a calm cat, but a top-loading or multi-door design, like the Howsehold or Frisco here, makes it far easier to lower a resistant cat in bottom-first, and lets a vet examine them without a full removal from the carrier.

guide.q: Do I need a crash-tested carrier for the car?
guide.a: If your cat travels in the car regularly, a crash-tested carrier like the Tavo Maeve here, certified to the UN ECE Child Restraint Standard, gives genuine extra protection in an accident. For occasional short trips to the vet, a standard secured carrier is usually sufficient.

guide.q: Should I cover the carrier when travelling?
guide.a: Many cats feel calmer with a light cover over part of the carrier, since it reduces visual stimulation and the stress of unfamiliar surroundings. Make sure ventilation isn't blocked, and remove the cover in warm conditions to avoid overheating.
